name: The Rain That Falls Upward
premise:
In a small plaza, raindrops rise from puddles toward the clouds. People are
reaching for their phones. The cheapest fix may be to explain the droplets,
not reverse them.

objective.description: Make the upward rain look coherent before the crowd records it.

anchors.name: storm_memory
anchors.description: The smell of rain from a childhood storm.

rain.observe_text:
Droplets rise from puddles. Reversing their gravity would fight a deep rule
in public.

vent.observe_text:
A street vent sits beside the puddles. A timed upward draft could make the
rising droplets look like spray.

mist.observe_text:
A maintenance nozzle nearby could add a street-cleaning mist, giving the
droplets an ordinary source.

phones.observe_text:
Several phones are coming up. Camera masking helps records, but not human
eyes.

puddle.observe_text:
The puddle edge is wide. Moving the boundary changes where the anomaly is
visible, not why it makes sense.

upward.scene_message: The vent coughs upward. Rising droplets become spray in a gust, strange but believable.
upward.system_note: Context patch. The observation remains but gains a plausible cause.
upward.discovered_rule: Preserve the visible event when a local explanation is cheaper than reversal.

cleaning.scene_message: A cleaning mist starts with a mechanical hiss. The upward droplets are now part of the spray.

normal.scene_message: The rain snaps downward. Everyone blinks at the sudden correction.

smear.scene_message: Phone sensors smear the droplets into glare. The crowd can still see them.

narrow.scene_message: The puddle tightens inward. The upward rain is smaller, not explained.

upward_rain.text:
Reversing droplet gravity is expensive. A vent draft or cleaning mist can
make the same visible motion plausible.

scene_progression.message: The first videos upload before reality has an excuse.

hidden_rules: The cheapest fix can be contextual explanation, not reversal.
